content_units: This mix works best if it starts familiar and upbeat, climbs into high-energy dance tracks, hits a big singalong stretch, then eases out with warm, nostalgic songs. The songs you picked already fit that arc very well.
Phase   Artist   Song   Why it fits
Opening   Earth, Wind & Fire   September   Instantly recognizable, feel-good, and welcoming without peaking too early
Opening   ABBA   Dancing Queen   Cross-generational classic that gets people smiling and moving
Opening   Dua Lipa   Levitating   Modern disco-pop groove that keeps the room building naturally
Peak-energy   Mark Ronson ft. Bruno Mars   Uptown Funk   Big dancefloor payoff with broad age appeal
Peak-energy   WALK THE MOON   Shut Up and Dance   Fast, catchy, and ideal once the room is fully engaged
Peak-energy   The Weeknd   Blinding Lights   Drives momentum with a huge chorus and retro-pop energy
Singalong   The Killers   Mr. Brightside   One of the strongest group-sing moments for this age range
Wind-down   ABBA   Dancing Queen   If reused later in a shorter reprise/remix, it can soften the landing; otherwise swap with one of the suggested additions below
Note: since you only gave 7 songs, the wind-down section is a little thin; the added tracks below fill that naturally.
Five More Tracks That Match the Same Feel
1.   I Wanna Dance with Somebody   — Whitney Houston
- Perfect for either peak-energy or singalong
- Big feel-good lift with strong singalong value
- Great bridge from dancefloor to anthem section
3.   Can’t Stop the Feeling!   — Justin Timberlake
- Family-safe, upbeat, and easy for mixed-age groups
- Works well in opening or early peak-energy
- Nostalgic and playful for this demographic
5.   Valerie   — Mark Ronson ft. Amy Winehouse
- Great for wind-down while keeping the mood happy
